# Emergency Medicine
## Procedure
1. Stop massive external bleeding. 2. Check oxygen, blood, perfusion, and heart rhythm. 3. Enable oxygen support or ventilation. 4. If circulation is absent, perform CPR. 5. If the rhythm is shockable, use the defibrillator. 6. Restore blood volume. 7. Address the trauma source or systemic damage.
## CPR
- Item: empty hand. - Condition: the patient is lying down and has no circulation. - Use: click the patient with an empty hand. - Result: temporary assistive perfusion and slower brain damage.
## Ventilation
- Item: [color=#58e6d9]NCManualVentilator[/color]. - Use: use it on a patient with insufficient breathing. - Result: temporary support for ventilation and oxygenation.
## Crystalloid
- Item: [color=#58e6d9]NCCrystalloidBag[/color]. - Result: increases effective circulating volume.
## Blood
- Item: compatible [color=#58e6d9]Bloodpack[/color]. - Result: adds blood to the bloodstream solution and restores oxygen-carrying volume.
## Defibrillation
- Item: [color=#58e6d9]Defibrillator[/color]. - Condition: [color=#76e69a]Shockable arrest[/color] rhythm. - Result: attempt to restore a normal rhythm. - After the action: re-check rhythm, oxygen, and perfusion.
## Arrest states
- [color=#ffcc66]Clinical arrest[/color] — circulation has stopped, but the brain may still be viable. - [color=#ff5c5c]Brain dead[/color] — irreversible brain state.
